messages.text: Hi, my KBox has stopped working. How can I get an RMA?

Hi, I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your KBox over to me.

Before anything goes to a return, I need to work out what actually failed, since most "stopped working" cases turn out to be the power supply or firmware rather than the board.

One thing to start with: when you plug it in now, what does it do?

1. Any lights on the unit at all?
2. Do the fan(s) spin, even for a second?
3. Does it show up on your network / in the web UI, or nothing?

Tell me what you see and we will take it from there.

Hi, light on the unit / fans spin up / UI works as normal. Current draw from the wall is only 9 - 14W no matter what setting is used. The device shows on pools OK but with zero hashrate. Hashrate in both UI and front screen show zero no matter what setting. I have tried factory reset and using multiple different pools with same result. It ran fine for about 1.5 weeks before failing.

Thanks, that is a very useful description. It rules out the usual suspects already: the unit powers, the controller boots, the network and pool side are fine, and you have reset it. So the controller is alive and only the hashing side is dead.

The 9 to 14W is the key number. A healthy KBOX pulls far more than that under load, so that figure says the hashboard is not drawing core power at all, which usually means the chips are not being detected or enabled.

Two things from you, then I can tell which it is:

1. In the web UI, what does it report for the ASIC / chip count and the ASIC status or any error line (some builds show "0 chips" or a detection error)?
2. The firmware version shown in the UI.

A photo of the front screen and a screenshot of the UI overview page is ideal if that is easy.

If the chip count reads zero, this is a board-level issue and not something a setting will fix. If it reads the full count, a clean full reflash of the firmware is the next step and that often brings the chips back.
The firmware version is v1.20.0. The device states this is the latest version.

Good, firmware is current, so we can set that aside.

The one number I still need is the chip / ASIC count. On the KBOX UI it is on the main overview or status page, usually next to ASIC model or chip count, together with any status or error line.

What does it show there? "0" versus the full count decides this: zero means the hashboard is not being detected and no setting will fix it, a full count means we try a clean reflash from scratch rather than the in-UI update.

A screenshot of that page works too if it is easier than typing it out.
Not seeing a chip count in the UI.

That is fine, not every KBOX build exposes it.

Then we go by behaviour instead, and the behaviour already tells us a lot: latest firmware, factory reset, several pools, and the wall draw pinned at 9 to 14W at every setting. That is the unit sitting at controller-only power, with the hashing side never coming up.

Two last checks before I write this up:

1. Do you have another power supply of the same rating you can try, or a different known-good cable and wall socket? A supply that has lost its ability to deliver current under load can look exactly like this, and it is the one cheap cause left.
2. A photo of the front screen as it runs, and a clear photo of the serial number label on the unit.

If a second supply makes no difference, the fault is on the board itself and I will pass my findings to the team with everything we have done.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Handed back to Sarah with my findings.
